task.description: CHANGE-APPROACH REWORK (ORCHESTRATOR.md Section 5's change-approach rule): the SAME root cause has now failed Step Final twice in a row with different files each time -- main keeps moving (WF03-ISS0261-20260822 then WF03-ISS0260-20260822, both already-merged, unrelated runs) faster than the per-file @grandfathered list added in this run's original design can keep up with, because H6 is new and every non-JSON/malformed handoff file that has EVER existed anywhere in handoffs/ history becomes a violation the instant H6 ships, regardless of when it was created. Repeating the identical strategy (add N more exact-path entries, retry merge, discover N more) is not a fix -- it will recur indefinitely as long as any other run is concurrently landing handoff files on main. REDESIGN the grandfathering mechanism for H6 specifically (leave H1-H4's existing per-file @grandfathered entries and mechanism untouched) as a COMMIT-BOUNDARY rule instead of a per-file list, mirroring this same file's own EXISTING precedent: @artifacts_out_rule_commit (a named commit sha used as a floor, resolved via `git show -s --format=%cI <sha>`, compared against each handoff's created_at) already solves exactly this class of problem for the ARTIFACTS_OUT_SELF_REF advisory check. Design: H6 should NOT fire on a non-JSON handoff-shaped file whose file content already existed in git history (i.e. was already committed to a commit that is an ancestor of, or equal to, a named 'H6 introduction' floor commit) BEFORE this fix's own H6 check was introduced -- state precisely how to determine 'already existed before the floor' for a file (first-commit-touching-this-path via `git log --follow --diff-filter=A -- <path>` or equivalent, compared against the floor commit's timestamp or ancestry) since, unlike ARTIFACTS_OUT_SELF_REF's created_at-inside-the-JSON approach, a non-JSON file has no created_at field to read -- git history is the only source of truth here. A file first added to git AFTER the floor commit must still hard-fail H6 (that is the entire point of the original ISS-0262 fix: catch NEW non-JSON handoffs going forward). State the exact floor commit to use (the commit that will land THIS fix, i.e. cannot be known until it lands -- consider whether the floor should instead be 'the moment ORCH's Step Final actually runs', using this run's own branch point or HEAD's parent commit at merge time, and how that interacts with squash-merge; state your reasoning and pick one mechanically well-defined choice). Update the existing 10+2 grandfathered path entries: decide whether they can now be REMOVED from the explicit list (superseded by the boundary rule) or must remain as a documented example/regression-test fixture -- do not leave both mechanisms silently overlapping without stating which one governs.
acceptance_criteria: Design states the exact mechanism for determining a file's git-history introduction point, with a concrete command/algorithm, not just prose intent

Design states the exact floor-commit choice and justifies it against the squash-merge timing problem (the floor commit literally cannot name itself, same constraint HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's own commit_sha_list section already documents for a different field -- read that section's reasoning and either reuse it or state why it doesn't transfer)
Design states the disposition of the existing 12 @grandfathered H6 entries under the new rule (removed, or kept as documented precedent/test fixtures) -- no silent overlap
Design explicitly re-verifies: a handoff file added to git AFTER the floor must still hard-fail H6 (this is checked, not assumed)
This design does not touch or weaken H1-H4's existing per-file @grandfathered mechanism

result.summary: CHANGE-APPROACH rework per ORCHESTRATOR.md Sec.5: redesigned H6's grandfathering as a commit-boundary rule instead of a per-file list, per task.description. New file lib/letflow/design/iss0262-h6-floor-commit-addendum.md (supersedes only Sec.3/Sec.3.1 of the original design; Sec.1,2,4.1-4.3,4.5,5,6,7 of the original still govern). Mechanism: new module attribute @h6_floor_commit (a git sha, resolved the same way @artifacts_out_rule_commit already is); new pre_floor_file?/2 that (a) finds a path's first-ever git appearance via `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%H --reverse -- <path>` (empty output = not yet in history = fails safe to not-pre-floor), then (b) checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor <first_add_sha> <floor>` -- exit 0 means the file's content already existed at/before the floor (grandfathered, hard_grandfathered not hard_new), non-0/error means it postdates the floor or git failed (fails safe to hard_new, opposite fail-safe direction from the existing advisory ARTIFACTS_OUT_SELF_REF check, justified in addendum Sec.1.4 because H6 is a hard gate). lint_file/2's :non_json branch now calls pre_floor_file?/2 instead of grandfathered?("H6", path); grandfathered?/2 itself and the 6 H1/H2/H3 @grandfathered entries are untouched. Floor-commit choice (addendum Sec.2): the pre-merge tip of origin/main, captured at GIT_MERGE.md step 4's fetch and written into @h6_floor_commit as an ordinary content commit before step 5's checks, refreshed on every Step Final retry -- NOT this fix's own squash-merge commit sha, which structurally cannot be known at write time (same class of problem HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's commit_sha_list section documents at :464-572, 'a commit cannot record its own sha'). Read that section in full: its resolution for a value that must live INSIDE the very artifact it references is an optional write-back second commit that records only the predecessor, never itself (:524). H6's floor does NOT have that self-containment property (it lives in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, a file disjoint from the handoffs/ files H6 classifies -- addendum Sec.2.2), so no write-back commit is needed at all: using the already-existing pre-merge origin/main tip (the commit immediately before the not-yet-existing squash commit) sidesteps the self-reference problem structurally rather than solving it via extra commits. Sec.2.3 states the exact operational fetch-then-set-attribute step for whoever runs the next Step Final attempt, and Sec.2.4/Sec.6 item 3 explicitly re-verify (with a worked example and a concrete test construction using real repo commits, not asserted) that a file introduced on main AFTER the floor still lands in hard_new. Disposition of the 12 existing {"H6", path} @grandfathered entries (10 original + 2 from the retry-1 rework): REMOVED, not kept -- addendum Sec.3/Sec.3.1 gives the exact deletion and the replacement dated comment; grandfathered?/2 is never called with "H6" again post-fix, so no overlap between the old list and the new rule is left in place. Also added a short superseded-pointer note at the top of the original design doc's Sec.3 so the two documents cannot be read as silently disagreeing. Original design's Sec.4.5 moduledoc bullet for H6 is restated in addendum Sec.4 to describe the commit-boundary mechanism instead of per-file grandfathering. No implementation code in either document -- module-attribute declaration, @spec lines, two git command literals, and case/pseudocode control-flow shapes only.
result.next_action: ORCH routes to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate this addendum before ELIXIR-DEV implements Sec.1/Sec.2/Sec.3/Sec.4 of lib/letflow/design/iss0262-h6-floor-commit-addendum.md in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, then a further Step Final retry resumes from GIT_MERGE.md step 4 on this same branch, performing addendum Sec.2.3's fetch-then-set-@h6_floor_commit operational step before running post-rebase checks.
